title: Only part sales created after release charge the core from the quote
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner/Admin user (that role holds every permission, including Part sales - Create & Edit).
  • A customer to sell to exists.
  • The pre-release sale: a part sale started BEFORE the release with a core (created before the Founder Mode release reached this build, for example dated Sep 30, 2026 or earlier), whose parts list shows a "Core for ..." row.
  • The newly-created sale: a NEW part sale seeded now for the customer with the part "Water Pump" (Quantity 1, Vendor = a test vendor, Sell Price $517.55, Core Charge $79.99), not Authorized or Ordered.
  • A sale you can split and two part sales you can move a line between.
custom_steps:
1. On the pre-release sale, open the Finance tab estimate and check whether the core shows before the part is received.
  2. On the newly-created sale, check the estimate shows the Core charge from the quote.
  3. Tick the part line on the new sale and use the menu ( ... ) above the parts list -> Split Part Sale (the new sale opens straight away), and check whether the resulting sale still charges the core from the quote.
  4. Move the line to another part sale (tick it, menu ( ... ) above the parts list -> Move Part -> pick the Part Sale -> Move) and check the core treatment after the move.
  5. Confirm no existing sale changed on release day.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The pre-release sale keeps the total it was quoted at - its core appears only when the part is received; the newly-created (post-release) sale shows the Core charge from the moment it is quoted.
  • A split follows the sale it was split from, and Move Part keeps the core treatment of the sale the line came from, whichever sale it lands on - a split or move never adds or removes a core charge.
  • No data was migrated and nothing an existing sale shows changed on release day; the new behaviour reaches only sales started from the release onward.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10262 (Story 1, Return a core on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 1; design canvas boards Cores_*/Document_*; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R21: “Only sales started on or after the release charge a core from the quote ... What decides is when the sale was created ... A sale split from another sale follows the sale it was split from, not when it was itself created. A split never changes whether a line's core is charged from the quote. Move Part works the same way between part sales: a moved line keeps the core treatment of the part sale it came from”
  • S1-N4: “No data is migrated and no amount already billed is rewritten ... Nothing an existing sale shows changes on release day ... The new behavior reaches sales started from the release onwards”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.
